name: Messaging
summary: Bind a session to your own imessage conversation: text it what to do from your phone, and let it text you back. A text never goes into an open dialog; it waits and arrives once the dialog closes.
description: Carnivore connects to a messaging provider (the imsg bridge, speaking the Carnivore Provider Protocol) and binds sessions to conversations, in, out or both. A text from you reaches the bound session: a threaded reply goes to the session that sent the original, a leading @name to that session, otherwise the default one; with several bound and none named, Carnivore texts back which session. Only your own handles, as imessage, are accepted; an sms gets a short reply asking for imessage, and a stranger gets nothing. While a permission, question or startup dialog is open the text is held and you get one text saying so; it goes in when the dialog closes, and several held texts arrive as one batch, oldest first, each dated. An asleep session is woken. An edit or unsend replaces or drops a held text, and sends a short note after delivery. A bound session sends with messaging_send: text only, secrets starred, rate limited, and logged first. Secrets live in the keychain only, and the provider's address is write-only.
where: Settings, notifications, messaging: providers, their conversations, every binding and the message log.
how_to: Open settings, notifications, messaging and press add provider. Enter the bridge address, its token (or an op:// reference) and your phone number or email; allow a private address and plain http only for a bridge on your own network. Save: Carnivore checks the bridge first.
On the provider, press add conversation and add the conversation with you; only conversations the bridge lists as routable can be added.
Ask an agent with the messaging tools to bind the session to the conversation (it names a direction: in and out, in only or out only); you approve the bind when it asks.
Text the conversation from your phone. Start with @name to reach one session when several are bound, or reply to a session's own text.
Watch the log on the settings screen for held and failed messages; retry a failed one there.
A text you sent whose outcome is unknown (the bridge restarted mid-send) shows in the log as unconfirmed, in its own color, with no retry: check your phone before sending it again.
On the provider card, the duplicate-send protection line says whether a retried send was ever answered with the original result (proven, with when) or never seen yet.
examples: You text restart the feed while the session is asking a permission question; you get held for ledgerbot, and the text goes in after you answer the dialog.
Three texts sent while the computer was asleep arrive as one message, oldest first, each with its time and age.
A bound session texts you build is green with messaging_send; a session without an out binding is refused.
media_exempt: The screen's media are captured at the next version bump with the rest of the feature recapture.
